🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Three Taddei Appointees Out as Blanca Cruz Takes Over the INE</u>

Mexico's electoral institute has a new interim president. Councillor Blanca Cruz García took the INE's top seat after Guadalupe Taddei's resignation, and the first thing she announced was a review of every senior official. Three resigned on day one, among them Mario Alfonso Burciaga Esparza, head of Material Resources, the office that handles the contracts now under audit. Cruz promised to restore collegial decision-making and to make it easy for investigators to do their job.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Cuba: Mexico and Havana Working to Restart Pemex Oil Shipments</u>

Cuba's ambassador to Mexico, Eugenio Martínez Enríquez, says the two countries are working to resume Mexican oil and fuel shipments to the island, which were halted in 2026 under Trump's tariff threats. The supply ran through a commercial contract between Pemex and a Cuban company, and Cuba paid regularly. "Work is under way to resume those energy shipments," he told EFE, as reported by El Financiero. By late 2025, Mexico was one of Cuba's main fuel suppliers.
banner: CUBA: PEMEX OIL SHIPMENTS MAY RESUME

🇲🇽🚛 <u>Truckers' Blockades End: Gobernación Closes a Deal With Canacar</u>

After a long negotiating session, Gobernación reached an agreement with Canacar and other freight organizations: highway blockades are definitively lifted and protests suspended. At its peak the stoppage had 38 protest points in 19 states, with 691 vehicles and 858 participants. Security, infrastructure, tax, social security and labor demands now go to a dialogue table run by Gobernación. This was one day after Canacar's leadership met with Alito Moreno and turned down talks.

🇲🇽🔍 <u>Mexico City: Disappearances Down 30%, Locations Up 68%</u>

Missing-person reports in Mexico City fell 30% between 2024 and 2026, while the number of people located each week rose 68%, Clara Brugada reported. 98% of cases end with the person found alive, half of them within 24 hours, and 1,204 people from reports filed before 2025 have been located. The city put 460 million pesos into search work and signed 21 new commitments with search collectives, on top of 30 that are 83% complete.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Congress Summons the INE's Comptroller Over Taddei-Era Contracts</u>

The Chamber of Deputies' Jucopo voted unanimously to summon Víctor Hugo Carvente, head of the INE's Internal Control Body, to explain his investigations into the institute's contracts. The UIF, SAT and FGR are already probing conflicts of interest tying former INE officials to Cajas Graf, Formas Finas y Materiales, Corporativo Zeg and Comercializadora JVYL. "Transparency is what best suits the country," said Ricardo Monreal.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Amnesty International Is Co-opted</u>

After several collectives backed the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances' intervention on Mexico, Sheinbaum rejected the idea that the committee's assessment was impartial. Amnesty International, she said, "is also co-opted by those who are against the Government of Mexico" and wants to hold more events here. Starting Wednesday, Gobernación resumes its dialogue tables with the mothers searching for the disappeared.

🇲🇽🇧🇷 <u>Sheinbaum and Lula Trade Invitations After His Re-election</u>

Claudia Sheinbaum called Lula da Silva after he won Brazil's runoff, and the two left-wing presidents of Latin America's two largest economies agreed to visit each other. "I invited him to come to Mexico. He invited me to go to Brazil," Sheinbaum said, adding that they will speak again to set the dates and agenda for both visits.

🔥🇲🇽 "There is dialogue. But what there cannot be is the defense of privileges." "It draws attention that three days ago they meet with the president of the PRI, the very same ones who called the strike yesterday. Now, really, draw your own conclusions." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 A faction of the trucking chamber Canacar blocked highways on Monday, even though talks with the Interior Ministry were already open. Today it agreed to talk. The dispute is over a tax break: a very small group of large carriers deducts toll payments at least twice, worth more than 5 billion pesos. López Obrador capped the benefit at companies with up to 300 million pesos in income; the Finance Ministry now lowers the cap to 250 million. "Most truckers are not mobilizing," Sheinbaum said.
